title: PoinnCARE: Hyperbolic Multi-Modal Learning for Enzyme Classification
claim: Entities carry a multi-level hierarchical label, and the functional label depends on a small localized region of the structure.
layout: Single panel: structure top-left with arrow, stacked hierarchy boxes below
description: A single illustrative example of one enzyme. At top left is a beige 3D molecular surface rendering of a protein, with a small red-orange patch marking the active site. A black arrow runs from that patch to the label 'Active site'. At top right, large text reads 'P49183 in UniProt with EC 3.1.21.1'. Below, four full-width rectangular boxes with dark teal borders are stacked vertically. Each gives one level of the EC hierarchy, from EC 3: Hydrolases through EC 3.1: Acting on ester bonds and EC 3.1.21: Endodeoxyribonucleases producing 5'-phosphomonoesters to EC 3.1.21.1: deoxyribonuclease I. In each box the newly specified digit of the EC number is red. The eye goes first to the protein and its red active site, then down the hierarchy boxes.
caption: An example enzyme.
abstract: Enzyme Commission (EC) number prediction is vital for elucidating enzyme functions and advancing biotechnology applications. However, current methods struggle to capture the hierarchical relationships among enzymes and often overlook critical structural and active site features. To bridge this gap, we introduce PoinnCARE, a novel framework that jointly encodes and aligns multi-modal data from enzyme sequences, structures, and active sites in hyperbolic space. By integrating graph diffusion and alignment techniques, PoinnCARE mitigates data sparsity and enriches functional representations, while hyperbolic embedding preserves the intrinsic hierarchy of the EC system with theoretical guarantees in low-dimensional spaces. Extensive experiments on four datasets from the CARE benchmark demonstrate that PoinnCARE consistently and significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in EC number prediction.
